solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Ingenious mechanical device by entrance to castle

indicators.note: the entrance to something is its front, so only the opening letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: a lever is a simple mechanical device for shifting loads

explanation.surface: A clever gadget is installed beside the gateway of a castle.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone or something showing inventive skill; plain synonyms.

clue.text: What you'd get from a keg with ale bursting out?

definitions.text: What you'd get from a keg with ale bursting out?

indicators.note: bursting out suggests violent disruption, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking what happens when beer escapes from a broken barrel.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines and builds: A, KEG and ALE rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Ale escaping from a cask is a spill or seepage of its contents.

clue.text: Zealously loving couple initially going out made a mark?

indicators.note: a couple of the first letters leave, so two opening letters are removed

parts.note: devoted means loving zealously

explanation.surface: A doting pair leave early after leaving their initials somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'couple initially going out' removes the first two letters, DE, from DEVOTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Voting is done by putting a cross on a ballot paper, so a voter has made a mark.

clue.text: Brought back as a spruced up item of furniture?

definitions.meaning: retrieved or regained, brought back from loss

definitions.text: a spruced up item of furniture?
definitions.meaning: a sofa given new upholstery has been covered again

explanation.surface: An old armchair brought back to life by new upholstery.
explanation.definitionFit: Means regained, and also, split as re-covered, describes a chair given fresh fabric.

clue.text: Way to gain speed within reason

parts.note: a mode is a way or manner of doing something
rate means speed, as in a rate of knots

explanation.surface: Advice on how to accelerate without going too far.
explanation.definitionFit: Something kept within reason is not excessive, which is what the adjective means.

clue.text: Poles gathering round one, old-style Communists?

indicators.note: gathering means taking in, so the poles enclose the other pieces

parts.note: masts are tall poles
a round shape is the letter O
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Polish people crowd around a lone old Communist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like the nationality but means MASTS; 'gathering' puts O and I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Followers of Mao Zedong's version of communism, a now dated strand of it.

clue.text: Composer unhappy, upset about country not his

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the turned word goes round the country
upset means overturned, so the word is read from the end backwards

parts.note: sad means unhappy
the UK is a country not the French composer's own

explanation.surface: A composer is miserable and upset over a foreign country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns the word for unhappy round, and 'about' wraps it round the country. Paul Dukas was French, so Britain is not his country.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Dukas was a French composer, best known for The Sorcerer's Apprentice.

clue.text: Once again look at way of restraining half of those watching the match

parts.note: a rein is used to restrain a horse

indicators.note: only half the word is kept, the latter part being cut away

parts.note: spectators watch a match

explanation.surface: A way of keeping half the crowd at a match under control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' keeps SPECT, the first half of SPECTATORS.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect again is to look at something once more; the prefix re- means again.

clue.text: Piling up in arena after match

indicators.note: after puts the arena word following the match word

parts.note: a tie is a cup match
a boxing ring is an arena

explanation.surface: Things stacking up in a stadium once the game is over.
explanation.definitionFit: Arranging in tiers is stacking in rows one above another, a piling up.

clue.text: How one may spin round having drunk cocktails and wine!

indicators.note: drunk suggests something reeling and muddled, so the letters of the two drinks are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone who has had cocktails and wine is left spinning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having drunk' looks like the drinker's state; 'drunk' is the signal to rearrange COCKTAILS and WINE, thirteen letters in all.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinning round against the direction a clock's hands move is the sense of the adverb.

clue.text: Mum enjoys life touring round 500 islands

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mum

indicators.note: touring round means going all the way about, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: someone who lives enjoys life to the full
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

explanation.surface: A mother who loves life makes a tour of hundreds of islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touring round' makes the life word go round the Roman 500, after the word for mum.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian Ocean republic is an archipelago made up of many small coral islands.

clue.text: Bird hide is to be concealed

indicators.note: a word concealed sits tucked inside another, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: an animal's hide is its skin

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher's hide is to be kept out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hide' looks like a birdwatcher's shelter, but it is an animal's hide, and 'to be concealed' tucks 'is' inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A small yellow-green finch, so a specific example of a bird.

clue.text: Characters involved in quite a serious problem

indicators.note: Characters involved in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people are caught up in a rather grave difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: A brain-teaser is a puzzle, a tricky problem to solve; a synonym.

clue.text: One working at court?

parts.note: looks like a lawyer or courtier, but a court is also a plain low-cut lady's shoe, so this is someone who makes such footwear

explanation.surface: Someone employed at a law court or royal court.
explanation.walkthrough: A court shoe is a woman's plain high-heeled shoe in British English.
explanation.definitionFit: A cobbler makes all kinds of footwear, court shoes among them; a punning cryptic sense.

clue.text: Wise person gathering speed as befits our modern era?

indicators.note: gathering means taking in and holding, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: a sage is a wise person
pace means speed

explanation.surface: A wise old person picks up speed, as is fitting nowadays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gathering' puts the speed word inside the wise person; the definition reads the answer as an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, the phrase means ultra-modern, typical of the era of rockets and satellites.

clue.text: Gear, as put out for soldier to wear

indicators.note: to wear is to have on, so the shuffled letters go around the soldier
out means not in order, so the two words are shuffled

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper, a soldier

explanation.surface: Kit is laid out for a soldier to put on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges 'as put' into APTUS, and 'to wear' puts the soldier inside it, after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparatus means equipment, the gear needed for a task.

clue.text: Lawyer giving advice to those who'll miss live broadcast of Opening of Parliament?

definitions.meaning: in Britain a part-time judge, usually a barrister, holds this title

definitions.text: giving advice to those who'll miss live broadcast of Opening of Parliament?
definitions.meaning: the advice is to tape her, the monarch, who opens Parliament

explanation.surface: A lawyer tells people who can't watch the State Opening live to tape it.
explanation.walkthrough: The State Opening of Parliament is performed by the British monarch; the clue dates from a queen's reign, so 'record 'er' is the advice.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior barrister sitting as a part-time judge in English courts bears this title; the second sense is a pun on taping her.

clue.text: The Spanish wine, cold and 'springy'

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
Asti is a sparkling Italian wine
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A Spanish wine served cold has some bounce.
explanation.definitionFit: Elastic material springs back into shape, so the adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: What gardener manages having no time for 14 science?

indicators.note: having none of something means it is taken away from the word

parts.note: the science of the space age, as entry 14 puts it, is rocketry

explanation.surface: Asking what a gardener looks after when too busy for modern science.
explanation.walkthrough: Entry 14 is SPACE AGE, whose science is ROCKETRY; 'having no' removes its T.
explanation.definitionFit: A gardener tends a rock garden, a feature of stones and alpine plants.

clue.text: Liquid nourishment that's knocked back for example at work

indicators.note: knocking back a drink tips it up, so the letters built here are read in reverse order

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A drink that gets downed at the office, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' turns the whole run EGATOP round; it looks like drinking, which suits liquid nourishment.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick French-style soup, which is nourishment taken in liquid form.

clue.text: Complained, finding duck in garden wandering around

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the zero goes within the jumbled letters
wandering means straying aimlessly, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone moaned upon finding a duck roaming in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering around' rearranges GARDEN, and 'in' puts O (duck, a zero score in cricket) inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Groaning is making a low sound of complaint, so to complain in that way.

clue.text: After damage mum must get rid of her rodent

parts.note: to mar is to damage or spoil

indicators.note: getting rid of something removes it, so these letters are dropped from the word before

parts.note: mum is a word for mother
taken as written

explanation.surface: After some breakage, a mother is told to throw out her pet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must get rid of' strips HER from MOTHER, leaving MOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A large burrowing ground squirrel of mountain regions, so a kind of rodent.

clue.text: Heading for the championship

definitions.meaning: a heading at the top of a chapter or article
a sporting crown won by the champion

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a caption at the top of a page and a championship won in sport.

clue.text: Eccentric person, a mum in America's added spice

parts.note: a card is an amusing or eccentric person
mom is the American spelling of mum

explanation.surface: An odd character and an American mother have added a spice to the dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Aromatic seeds of an Indian plant used in curries and baking: an example of a spice.

clue.text: Saw a duke get older

parts.note: to age is to get older

explanation.surface: Someone spotted a duke growing old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like a verb but is the noun for a proverb.
explanation.definitionFit: An old saw is a proverb, so the two nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Use public transport across Sweden's capital to relieve pressure?

indicators.note: one phrase stretched across another holds it inside

parts.note: to take the train is to use public transport

indicators.note: the capital of a word is its first letter, its head

explanation.surface: Travelling by rail through Stockholm is a way to ease stress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like Stockholm but gives S, which 'across' places inside the rail phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear a load so another need not is to relieve the pressure on them; an idiom.

clue.text: Hardly seeing defacement around cathedral

parts.note: a scar is a mark that defaces
c, short for circa, means around
Ely is an English city with a famous cathedral in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: Barely noticing the vandalism on a cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: ELY is a cathedral city in eastern England; C stands for circa, around.
explanation.definitionFit: Both adverbs mean only just, almost not at all; plain synonyms.

clue.text: Firm prepared to put leader out on street

indicators.note: putting the leader out removes the front letter of the word before

parts.note: ready means prepared

explanation.surface: A company is ready to oust its boss on the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to put leader out' drops the first letter of the word for prepared, giving EADY, which follows the street abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Firm and steady both describe something stable and not shaking; synonyms.
